name: com.mikefluff/mikefluff
title: Mike Fluff
description: Mike Fluff Press books and their discussion, the business diagnostic, AI-text check, call booking.

tools.name: search_answers
tools.description: Search the answers Mike Fluff Press publishes (questions about crypto history, Bitcoin, stablecoins, fraud, AI agents, software after AI: "what happened to FTX", "who is Satoshi", "what is MCP") and the interactive experiments from the books. Use this first whenever the user asks a factual question these books cover. Returns up to 8 hits, each with the title, a 40-60 word lead answer you can quote, the canonical URL, the book, and the chapter it draws on. Read-only.

query.description: The question or keywords, in any of the four languages.

locale.description: Language of the results. Defaults to the language the query is written in.

tools.name: get_answer
tools.description: Fetch one published answer by its id (from search_answers): the full direct answer, the explanatory sections, the FAQ, the chapters and experiments it cites and related answers, all with canonical URLs. Use after search_answers when the lead answer is not enough. Read-only.

locale.description: Language of the result: en, ru, pt or es.

tools.name: list_books
tools.description: List the books by Mike Fluff Press with title, subtitle, synopsis, status, canonical book page URL and the table of contents (which chapters are free to read). Use it to answer "what has Mike Fluff written" or before get_chapter_preview. Read-only.

locale.description: Language of the result: en, ru, pt or es.

tools.name: get_chapter_preview
tools.description: Return the text of one chapter. Free chapters come back in full. A paid chapter comes back whole to an account that owns it (the book, or the chapter bought with buy_chapter) when the call carries its token; to anybody else as its public lead-in only (about a fifth of the chapter), with what the chapter costs on its own. Get book slugs and chapter ids from list_books. Read-only.

locale.description: Language of the result: en, ru, pt or es.

tools.name: run_diagnostic
tools.description: The self-diagnostic from mikefluff.com/diagnostic: ten multiple-choice questions about how a business runs, scored into one of five named operational conditions (e.g. "one queue, one person", "manual conveyor", "SaaS obesity") with a severity, an annual cost estimate built only from the user's own answers, and a recommended next step with its URL. Call it with answers = {} first to get the questionnaire (question ids, option ids, which questions are conditional), ask the user, then call again with {questionId: optionId} (an array of option ids for multiple-choice questions). Read-only: nothing is stored or mailed.

answers.description: Question id → option id, or option ids for a multiple-choice question. {} returns the questionnaire.

locale.description: Language of the result: en, ru, pt or es.

tools.name: check_text
tools.description: Run the writer linter behind mikefluff.com/ai-text-checker on a text: it flags the stock phrases and rhythms readers recognise as machine-written ("in today's fast-paced world", "it's important to note", em-dash habits in Russian) and returns a density verdict (clean / borderline / neuroslop suspected), a pass/fail gate for hard bans, and each hit with line, column, category and the matched words. English and Russian only. Up to 20000 characters. It judges the text, not who wrote it. Read-only: the text is not stored.

text.description: The text to check (plain text or Markdown).

lang.description: Language of the text: en or ru.

tools.name: get_booking_slots
tools.description: List the open 30-minute slots for a free video call with Mike Fluff (business diagnosis, AI automation, compliance, Architect Mode), as ISO 8601 UTC start times. Use before book_call; pass one of these exact values as its "slot". Read-only.

from.description: Earliest day to list, ISO date or date-time (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to now.

days.description: How many days to cover from "from". Default 7, at most 21.

locale.description: Language for the booking page URL. Default en.

tools.name: book_call
tools.description: SIDE EFFECT: books a real 30-minute video call in Mike Fluff's calendar, emails a confirmation with a calendar invite to the given address, alerts Mike, and records the booking as a lead. Only call this when the user has explicitly asked to book and chosen the time. "slot" must be one of the exact values returned by get_booking_slots. Name and email: either the ones the user gave for this purpose, or leave them out and the call is booked in the name of the person signed in with INITE ID (OAuth scope "mikefluff:booking"; without a token such a call is answered with HTTP 401 and the client is sent to sign in). Topics: diagnostic (general business consultation), automation (AI automation), compliance (privacy/GDPR/LGPD around AI systems), architect-mode (the one-day intensive). The confirmation email has a link to move or cancel. Limited to 3 bookings per hour per caller and 2 upcoming calls per email.

slot.description: Exact ISO 8601 start time from get_booking_slots, e.g. 2026-10-20T13:00:00.000Z.

name.description: The user's name, as they gave it. Omit to use the signed-in account's name.

email.description: The user's email; the confirmation goes there. Omit to use the signed-in account's email.

message.description: Optional: what the user wants to discuss, in their words.

timeZone.description: Optional IANA time zone of the user (e.g. America/Sao_Paulo) for the email's times.

consent_ref.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the reference it gave you.

consent_code.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the six digits the person read to you. Never guess it.

tools.name: buy_course
tools.description: SIDE EFFECT: opens a checkout for one of Mike Fluff's paid courses and records the user as a lead. Returns a payment link (billing's hosted page; works without signing in) and the price in the currency for the locale. Nothing is charged until the user pays on that page; after payment the course access link is emailed to the given address. Courses: parasites (parasites-course), freeMini (vibe-coding-course), contentFactory (content-factory-course). Only call when the user has asked to buy and given the email the course should go to — or leave the email out to use the account of the person signed in with INITE ID (OAuth scope "mikefluff:purchase"; with that scope the course is also attached to their account). Give the user the payment link; do not try to pay.

locale.description: Language and currency of the checkout.

email.description: The user's email; the access link is sent there after payment. Omit to use the signed-in account's.

tools.name: buy_book
tools.description: SIDE EFFECT, MAY SPEND MONEY: buys a Mike Fluff Press book for the person signed in with INITE ID. Books are bought into an INITE account (the reader unlocks paid chapters for the account that paid), so this needs the person: OAuth scope "mikefluff:purchase"; without a token it is answered with HTTP 401 and the client signs the person in. If the person has allowed this shop to charge their INITE wallet, the book is paid at once within the limit they set. If not, the result is one link for the person: there they pay this time and, if they like, allow such payments from now on. Failing both, a payment link (card, PIX). An agent signed in as itself (client_credentials, its own did:web) buys under its own account and pays the returned x402Url from its INITE wallet (pay tool at billing.inite.ai/mcp/wallet). If they already own the book it says so instead. Only call when the user has asked to buy this book.

locale.description: Language of the book page and currency of the price.

email.description: Optional: the user's email, for the receipt when the account has none.

consent_ref.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the reference it gave you.

consent_code.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the six digits the person read to you. Never guess it.

tools.name: buy_chapter
tools.description: SIDE EFFECT, MAY SPEND MONEY: buys one paid chapter of a Mike Fluff Press book, on its own, for whoever the token speaks for (OAuth scope "mikefluff:purchase"; without a token, HTTP 401 and the client signs the person in). The chapter is then theirs to read on the site and whole through get_chapter_preview. Paid the same ways as buy_book: from the person's INITE wallet where they allowed this shop, else one link for them (wallet or card/PIX); an agent signed in as itself pays the returned x402Url from its own INITE wallet (pay tool at billing.inite.ai/mcp/wallet). Owning the book already includes every chapter. Get chapter ids from list_books. Only call when the user has asked to buy this chapter.

locale.description: Language of the chapter and currency of the price.

email.description: Optional: the user's email, for the receipt when the account has none.

consent_ref.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the reference it gave you.

consent_code.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the six digits the person read to you. Never guess it.

tools.name: get_chapter_discussion
tools.description: Return the published reader comments on one chapter of a Mike Fluff Press book: who wrote, the quoted passage, the text, replies (parent_id), likes, and a link to the place in the chapter; comments by the author are marked. Open for chapters the caller may read, by the site's own rules (send the reader's token for chapters that need one). Read-only.

lang.description: Edition (language of the text): each has its own discussion.

tools.name: post_comment
tools.description: SIDE EFFECT: publishes a comment, in the signed-in person's name, in the public discussion of one chapter, where other readers see it. Use only when the person asks to post it, with words they approved. Optional `quote` pins it to a passage (copy it exactly from the chapter); `reply_to` answers a comment from get_chapter_discussion. Every comment goes through the site's moderation: one it holds is shown to the author only, and the result says so. Needs sign-in with the mikefluff:discuss scope and a chapter the person may read. For a private remark to the author use send_note_to_author.

lang.description: Edition (language of the text): each has its own discussion.

body.description: The comment, as the person wants it published.

quote.description: An exact passage from the chapter the comment is about.

reply_to.description: Id of the comment this answers.

consent_ref.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the reference it gave you.

consent_code.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the six digits the person read to you. Never guess it.

tools.name: send_note_to_author
tools.description: SIDE EFFECT: emails the author a private note about one passage (a correction, a question, a remark) from the signed-in person, and keeps it in their notes on the site; the author can reply to the person's email. Use only when the person asks, with their words. `quote` must be copied exactly from the chapter (it finds the paragraph). Needs sign-in with the mikefluff:discuss scope and a chapter the person may read. Nothing is published.

lang.description: Edition (language of the text): each has its own discussion.

quote.description: The passage, exactly as it is in the chapter.

note.description: What the person wants to tell the author.

consent_ref.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the reference it gave you.

consent_code.description: Only when the tool asked for a code: the six digits the person read to you. Never guess it.

tools.name: get_author_inbox
tools.description: For the author only: the notes readers sent them and the comments that are hidden (held by moderation, or hidden by hand), newest first, each with a link to its place. Publish or hide with moderate_comment. Needs the author signed in with the mikefluff:author scope. Read-only.

limit.description: At most this many of each.

tools.name: moderate_comment
tools.description: SIDE EFFECT: for the author only. `publish` shows a hidden or held comment to every reader of the chapter; `hide` takes one down (it stays visible to the author). Ids come from get_author_inbox or get_chapter_discussion. Needs the author signed in with the mikefluff:author scope.
